reason: Yes for the definitional fix only, and I state plainly what that does not buy. The defect is textual, not statistical: Act 21 §5 requires the recorded tree hash to match the merged commit's tree for every change to records/, and the commit carrying records/suite-status.json cannot contain the hash of the tree it creates. Act 26 moved when the record is written and added a hash-chain audit; it did not change which commit the record attests, so the carrier commit is still a records/ change that cannot satisfy §5 literally. This Act says expressly which clauses it amends (§2's 'commit being merged' means the verified candidate; §1's scoped suite excludes the carrier), fixes the integration base as the current main tip with the candidate a direct child and one fast-forward, makes the predicate mechanically decidable, and forbids claiming execution proof from timestamps. I verified at this digest: both red-teams are byte-exact substrings of §8a and §8b, §9 answers O1-O5 and B1-B6, and the file hashes to the bound digest. I do NOT vote yes on the claim that this restores the compliance rate: the 1090+ unreadable entries are the checker not recognising Act 26's prelanding artefact, which is Executive implementation and needs no law; §5a(5) of the bill says exactly that, and I cited the Clerk's investigation before this ballot existed. O5 and B5 remain unresolved in the bill and I accept them: no red-main episode is attributed to this defect, and if the Clerk or Judiciary produces a written interpretation putting the carrier outside §5's change class while keeping exact candidate verification and implementing the §3 fixtures, this Act is unnecessary and I will withdraw it. Until such an instrument exists, the text remains unsatisfiable and the only alternatives are informal interpretation or this narrow amendment.
